---
title: AWS Bedrock
description: bedrock() — model-agnostic provider via AWS Bedrock's Converse API. One adapter covers Claude, Llama, Mistral, Titan, Mixtral on Bedrock.
---

> AWS Bedrock's Converse API is model-agnostic — same wire format whether you're calling Claude, Llama, Mistral, Titan, or Mixtral. agentfootprint's `bedrock()` factory wraps it as one `LLMProvider`. No format-specific code per model family.

## Install

```bash
npm install @aws-sdk/client-bedrock-runtime
```

Peer dep, lazy-required, optional. AWS credentials resolved via the SDK's normal chain (env, profile, IAM role).

Reaching the models through your organisation's gateway instead — an API-key header and the InvokeModel operation rather than AWS credentials and Converse? Use [`invokeModelGateway()`](doc:invoke-model-gateway).

## Use

```ts
import { Agent } from 'agentfootprint';
import { bedrock } from 'agentfootprint/providers';

const provider = bedrock({
  region: 'us-east-1',
});

const agent = Agent.create({
  provider,
  model: 'anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929-v1:0',  // Bedrock-namespaced model id
}).build();
```

The model id is Bedrock's, not the upstream provider's. Cross-region inference profiles work as-is — just pass the profile id.

## Tools (Converse tool_use blocks)

Converse API's tool_use / tool_result blocks map cleanly to agentfootprint's `Tool[]` + `LLMMessage.toolCalls`. ReAct correctness preserved.

The mapping holds on **both** paths — `complete()` and `stream()` produce the same `toolCalls` for the same logical response, and a parity test pins them together so they cannot drift apart.

## Stream wait limits

Use `bedrock({ timeoutMs: 30_000 })` to bound a silent stream. The same cap
applies separately to the SDK response, each event read, an early close and
any non-stream fallback. It is an idle limit, not a total generation budget:
a stream that keeps making progress may run longer. Time while your code is
holding a yielded chunk does not count as provider silence.

<CodeFile path="examples/features/107-bedrock-stream-deadline.ts" region="timeout" title="Scripted timeout and recovery, no AWS calls" />

A miss raises `BedrockStreamTimeoutError` from `agentfootprint/providers`,
with `code: 'BEDROCK_STREAM_TIMEOUT'`, `phase` (`response`, `chunk`, `close` or
`fallback`), `timeoutMs` and `retryable: true`. `withRetry` retries only before
its first public chunk. Once a chunk reaches your code, a timeout surfaces
without replaying partial text. Mid-stream buffering/retry is not enabled by
this option.

Your request's `signal` still wins and keeps its cancellation reason. The
adapter passes the linked signal through the SDK's documented
[`abortSignal` option](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/developer/abortcontroller-in-modular-aws-sdk-for-javascript/),
requests iterator cleanup and refuses late results. Cancellation is best
effort: a timeout does not prove remote work stopped or tell you the bill.
Missing provider usage stays unknown.

Omitting `timeoutMs` keeps the existing uncapped stream behavior. A supplied
value must be positive, finite milliseconds, at most 2,147,483,647. It does
not add a timeout to direct `complete()` calls; use the caller's abort signal
or your run's time budget for those. The gateway and Bedrock implementations
use the same internal wait-deadline helper.

## Prompt caching

`bedrock()` declares caching **per model**. Pass the model to
`cacheStrategyFor(provider, model)` when attaching a cache meter; the Agent
resolves it automatically, including a model chosen by `.configure()` or a
skill brain. `withRetry`, `withCircuitBreaker` and `withFallback` preserve
this capability. Unknown IDs, custom aliases and profile ARNs have no
declared caching; the adapter sends no `cachePoint` for them. This is a
verified subset, not a statement that AWS cannot cache every omitted model.

<CodeFile path="examples/features/102-bedrock-prompt-cache.ts" region="cache" title="Two scripted calls, no AWS requests" />

The executable example uses a fake SDK, including a cache write on the first
call and a read on the second. These fixture counts prove the wiring;
they do not measure AWS latency or savings. A real request uses the normal
`bedrock({ region })` factory and your AWS credentials.

All listed models allow at most four checkpoints across the request. Claude
models accept them in `tools`, `system` and `messages`; Nova accepts `system`
and `messages` only. A marker becomes a separate union block after its exact
message or tool boundary. The port currently carries the composed system
prompt as one string, so a system marker covers that whole string. Skipped
messages never move a checkpoint onto a neighboring message.

`short` uses the default five-minute TTL. `long` becomes `ttl: '1h'` only
where the model documents it. Otherwise it is shortened to the default,
and a long checkpoint following a short one in wire order is shortened too;
prompt content is never reordered. Prefixes below the model's minimum may
complete without being cached. Cache writes can cost more than fresh input,
and repeated prompts do not guarantee a hit.

`minimumTokens` documents AWS's threshold; the adapter does not suppress
checkpoints using a token estimate. A below-minimum prefix does not cache:
the cache meter reports measured zero writes when AWS returns zero, rather
than pretending the provider measured nothing.

### Verified model facts

Checked against [AWS's caching guide](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/prompt-caching.html)
and its model cards. `bedrockModels.ts` is the single support table. Exact
geography profiles are allowed only where verified for that model; support
does not guarantee account access, region availability or a working bare
model endpoint. In particular, Haiku 4.5 on-demand calls require a documented
geography/global inference profile.

| Base model IDs | Minimum prefix | TTLs |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `anthropic.claude-haiku-5-5`, `anthropic.claude-sonnet-5-5`, `anthropic.claude-opus-5-5`, `anthropic.claude-fable-5-1`, `anthropic.claude-mythos-5-1`, `anthropic.claude-fable-5`, `anthropic.claude-mythos-5`, `anthropic.claude-opus-5` | 512 | 5 minutes, 1 hour |
| `anthropic.claude-opus-4-8`, `anthropic.claude-sonnet-5`, `anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6`, `anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929-v1:0` | 1,024 | 5 minutes, 1 hour |
| `anthropic.claude-opus-4-7`, `anthropic.claude-opus-4-6-v1`, `anthropic.claude-opus-4-5-20251101-v1:0`, `anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0` | 4,096 | 5 minutes, 1 hour |
| `anthropic.claude-3-7-sonnet-20250219-v1:0`, `anthropic.claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022-v2:0`, `anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-20250514-v1:0`, `anthropic.claude-opus-4-1-20250805-v1:0` | 1,024 | 5 minutes |
| `amazon.nova-2-lite-v1:0`, `amazon.nova-pro-v1:0`, `amazon.nova-lite-v1:0`, `amazon.nova-micro-v1:0` | 1K, as AWS states it; maximum 20K | 5 minutes |

The [API cache-point schema](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/APIReference/API_runtime_CachePointBlock.html)
defines `type: 'default'` and optional TTL. Both Converse and ConverseStream
report optional `cacheReadInputTokens` / `cacheWriteInputTokens`; the adapter
lifts these to `usage.cacheRead` / `cacheWrite`. Missing counts remain
unknown; a reported zero is measured zero. `usage.input` remains **fresh**
input, so the cache meter adds the three buckets once when calculating totals.

When an explicit cache policy cannot be honored, development mode warns once
per Agent build. A default policy warns only when the provider declares
model-aware caching but cannot cache the selected model. Ordinary Mock and
Ollama defaults are silent. Each run's existing
`agentfootprint.agent.run_configured` event includes only fixed cache
metadata with its source: `{ requested: 'explicit' | 'default', strategy: 'none', status: 'not-applicable' }`.
No prompt, policy function or provider configuration enters that field. The
manifest describes the default model; it does not claim every runtime model
override has the same support. `caching: 'off'` or all policies set to `never`
produces no warning or cache field.

Code that reads `provider.promptCaching.mode` directly must instead call
`promptCachingFor(provider, model)` from `agentfootprint/cache`, then inspect
the resolved declaration. The field can now be a model function; this is a
breaking TypeScript shape change. Existing static declarations still work.

## Thinking support

The current `bedrock()` Converse adapter does not implement the request and
response round-trip for thinking. It declares `thinkingMode: () => 'none'`:
`.thinking()` is refused at agent build, and direct `complete()` and
`stream()` calls with `req.thinking` fail before constructing or sending an
AWS command. The error is `UnsupportedThinkingError` with
`reason: 'no-thinking'`, not a successful call with the thinking request lost.

This is a limitation of this adapter, not of Amazon Bedrock itself. For a
supported Claude Messages route behind an InvokeModel gateway, use
[`invokeModelGateway()`](doc:invoke-model-gateway). Native Converse reasoning
support needs its own complete request/response implementation.

Forced tool choice is checked separately. The Converse adapter shares the
[Claude model restrictions](doc:anthropic#forced-tool-choice-is-model-specific);
normal requests without thinking are unchanged.

## Streaming

`provider.stream(req)` uses ConverseStream — text chunks land as they arrive, and the final chunk carries the authoritative `LLMResponse`.

Streamed tool calls **are** parsed. `bedrock()` accumulates the ConverseStream tool-use events — `contentBlockStart` (id + name), `contentBlockDelta` (JSON argument fragments), `contentBlockStop` — keyed by `contentBlockIndex`, so parallel tool calls whose fragments interleave are reassembled correctly. The completed calls arrive on the terminal chunk's `response.toolCalls`. Tools that take no arguments stream as `args: {}`.

Argument fragments are not yielded as chunks (`LLMChunk` has no field for them); they surface only on the terminal `response`.

<Callout type="warn">
**Honest by construction:** a response with `stopReason: 'tool_use'` and zero parsed tool calls is never returned quietly. The provider throws a `BedrockProviderError` with `code: 'BEDROCK_STREAM_TOOLUSE_LOST'` so a `reliability` rule can retry, instead of the agent confidently answering without running its tools.

**Fixed in 7.6.1.** Before this, `stream()` ignored the tool-use events entirely and returned `toolCalls: []` — an agent on `bedrock()` with streaming enabled silently produced a final answer instead of calling its tools. The non-streaming path was always correct.
</Callout>

## Production patterns

- AWS SDK handles credential refresh + region routing automatically.
- Wrap with `withRetry` (from `agentfootprint/resilience`) for transient throttling. The provider rethrows a `BedrockProviderError`; check `.code` to tell the failure classes apart:

| `.code` | Meaning | Extra fields |
|---|---|---|
| *(absent)* | Generic AWS transport / service error | `.status` — the AWS HTTP status code (`err.$metadata.httpStatusCode`) |
| `BEDROCK_STREAM_TOOLUSE_LOST` | `stopReason 'tool_use'` with zero parsed tool calls — a tripwire for future ConverseStream shape drift | — |
| `BEDROCK_MALFORMED_TOOL_ARGS` | The model emitted tool-argument JSON that does not parse. Thrown rather than swallowed to `{}`, so a tool is never executed with its arguments dropped | `.toolName`, `.toolUseId`, `.contentBlockIndex`, `.rawLength`, `.cause` |

  All three are retryable through `withRetry`. A retry usually recovers malformed tool-args JSON (the model re-emits it cleanly); `BEDROCK_STREAM_TOOLUSE_LOST` is a tripwire for persistent stream-shape drift, so if it repeats, report it rather than retrying harder.
- Tune the default model and token budget on the factory:

```ts
import { bedrock } from 'agentfootprint/providers';

const provider = bedrock({
  region: 'us-east-1',
  defaultModel: 'anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929-v1:0', // used when LLMRequest.model is the shorthand 'bedrock'
  defaultMaxTokens: 4096,
});
```

## Limitations

- Multi-modal not exposed yet (text content only).
- Bedrock Guardrails not exposed in the wrapper — pass via the SDK client directly if you need them.
